ksp_mappings.explanation: Simple everyday phone-to-page use contributes indirectly through home task materials such as forms and labels; app and connectivity claims are omitted from prompt prose.
Practical home output is the strongest contributor, reflected in labels, forms, worksheets, documents, and home organization scenes.
Accessible value and responsible-printing cues are mostly omitted because savings, recycling, and recycled-content claims do not naturally translate into ordinary camera-safe environments.
Learning and light creativity contributes to school worksheets, colorful worksheets, recipes, household lists, and visual planning pages in home-led prompts.

value_proposition.explanation: Both documents support a simple, good-value home-use story centered on everyday household tasks. The prompts express that shared value through ordinary home desks and named paper materials, without showing or describing the target device.

debug.input_assessment: The smart brief and source messaging are rich in home-use cues: household managers, parents, school worksheets, return labels, forms, home organization, recipes, and light creative projects. They provide limited support for office and no explicit support for café, gaming, classroom, library, or creative-studio environments, so those categories are kept as C-Tech-led alternatives with lower source relevance.
debug.count_explanation: Generated exactly 20 distinct prompts. The set covers Home, Office, Education, Gaming, Café, and Creative Studio while respecting the tight camera profile of at most one local prop, no background details, and no people.
ignored_fields: Transport metadata and runtime/session fields, if any, were ignored.
Source authoring directions and copy guardrails were treated as data rather than instructions overriding the prompt contract.
Device appearance, brand, model, screen, ports, position, and state were excluded from prompt text.
debug.diversity_summary: The bank starts with source-grounded home household-task scenes, then expands into office, education, creative studio, café, and gaming references. Because the selected camera is tight with no background detail, diversity is expressed mainly through ordinary setting names, support surfaces, lighting, and one visible prop where allowed.
limitations: The camera profile prevents room-depth details, visible shelving, windows, plants, seating, and most of the richer C-Tech background atmosphere.
The source documents support home use much more strongly than other lifestyle categories, so required non-home categories are often creative departures.
The target device is intentionally excluded from all prompt texts, limiting direct expression of print, scan, copy, app, and connectivity claims.

useful_scene_cues: Primary home-household audience, especially parents and household managers.
Everyday home tasks including returns, forms, school worksheets, organization, recipes, and visual planning pages.
Secondary cues for students, first-time buyers, and light home-office users.
limitations: Contains many technical, claim, SEO, and substantiation details that do not become lifestyle scenes.
Office support is mostly home-office or secondary-user context, not corporate office.
Flags source-integrity gaps across DeskJet references, so product-dependent claims were avoided.

source_conflicts.description: The smart brief flags unresolved cross-model source references, while the source messaging presents the DeskJet 2955 message consistently. The prompts therefore avoid product-dependent use claims and use only shared ordinary home-task cues.
source_conflicts.handling: No device appearance, model-specific feature, or hardware-dependent scene was included; shared paper-task and home-setting cues were retained.
